summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with type II diabetes and a history of depression and recurrent abscesses, was admitted after presenting with abdominal and perineal abscesses and diabetic ketoacidosis due to insulin non-adherence during a depressive episode. She was initially treated in the ICU with an insulin drip and IV fluids to resolve DKA. Surgical drainage and debridement of the abscesses were performed, and cultures grew methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus, Group B Streptococcus, and Streptococcus anginosus. Antibiotics were narrowed to oral cephalexin and levofloxacin. Her insulin regimen was changed to NPH due to hypoglycemia, and her Paxil dose was increased for depression. Acute kidney injury developed during admission, likely due to prerenal causes and acute tubular necrosis, and she was referred to nephrology for follow-up. She improved clinically, with stable vitals and resolving infection, and was discharged home with wound care support, oral antibiotics, and follow-up arranged for surgery, psychiatry, and kidney function monitoring.
problems: Diabetes with ketoacidosis, type II or unspecified type, uncontrolled
Acute kidney failure with lesion of tubular necrosis
Abscess of anal and rectal regions
Major depressive affective disorder, recurrent episode, moderate
